793:     try {
794:       this.persistentState = this.stateStore?.load() ?? this.persistentState;
795:       this.preferences = Object.fromEntries(
796:         Object.entries(this.persistentState.preferences).map(([capability, value]) => [
797:           capability,
798:           value?.mode ?? "auto",
799:         ]),
800:       );
801:       const [systemSeeds, managedSeeds, bundledSeeds] = await Promise.all([
802:         this.registry.collect(),
803:         this.paths && this.catalog
804:           ? managedSeedsFromState({
805:               paths: this.paths,
806:               state: this.persistentState,
807:               catalog: this.catalog,
808:               platform: this.platform,
809:               arch: this.arch,
810:             })
811:           : Promise.resolve([]),
812:         this.bundledCoreRoot && this.coreCatalog
813:           ? bundledSeedsFromResources({
814:               coreRoot: this.bundledCoreRoot,
815:               catalog: this.coreCatalog,
816:               platform: this.platform,
817:               arch: this.arch,
818:             })
819:           : Promise.resolve([]),
820:       ]);
821:       const customSeeds = Object.entries(this.persistentState.custom).flatMap(([capability, entry]) => {
822:         if (!entry) return [];
823:         const pathApi = this.platform === "win32" ? path.win32 : path.posix;
824:         const executable = normalizeToolPath(entry.executable, this.platform);
825:         if (!pathApi.isAbsolute(executable) || !this.fileSystem.isFile(executable)) return [];
826:         return [
827:           {
828:             capability: capability as ToolCapabilityId,
829:             provider: "custom" as const,
830:             discovery: "user-selected",
831:             executable,
832:             argvPrefix: [],
833:             binDir: pathApi.dirname(executable),
834:             rank: 0,
835:           },
836:         ];
837:       });
838:       const seeds = [...customSeeds, ...systemSeeds, ...bundledSeeds, ...managedSeeds, ...this.legacySearchSeeds];
839:       const groups = await mapConcurrent(seeds, this.probeConcurrency, async (seed) => {
840:         try {
841:           return await this.probe(seed, {
842:             platform: this.platform,
843:             arch: this.arch,
844:             env: this.env,
845:             tempRoot: this.tempRoot,
846:             fileSystem: this.fileSystem,
847:             executor: this.executor,
848:           });
849:         } catch {
850:           return [];
851:         }
852:       });
853:       const candidates = normalizeAndDedupeCandidates(groups.flat(), {
854:         platform: this.platform,
855:         resolveRealPath: (value) => this.fileSystem.realpath(value),
856:       });
857:       this.snapshot = this.createSnapshot(candidates, true, this.now().toISOString());
858:     } catch {
859:       this.snapshot = this.createSnapshot([], true, this.now().toISOString(), "TOOLCHAIN_INTERNAL");
860:     }
861:     this.resolutionCache.clear();
862:     for (const listener of [...this.listeners]) listener(this.snapshot);
863:     return this.snapshot;
864:   }

870:     lastErrorCode?: PublicToolchainState["lastErrorCode"],

934:   private buildComponentStates(
935:     candidates: readonly ToolCandidate[],
936:   ): Partial<Record<ManagedComponentId, PublicManagedComponentState>> {
937:     const result: Partial<Record<ManagedComponentId, PublicManagedComponentState>> = {};
938:     for (const componentId of ["portable-git", "node-lts", "cpython", "uv", "ripgrep", "fd", "jq", "bun"] as const) {
939:       const activation = this.persistentState.managed[componentId];
940:       const component = this.catalog?.components.find((entry) => entry.id === componentId);
941:       const variant = component?.variants.find((entry) => entry.platform === this.platform && entry.arch === this.arch);
942:       const healthy = candidates.some(
943:         (candidate) =>
944:           candidate.componentId === componentId &&
945:           candidate.provider === "managed" &&
946:           candidate.health === "healthy" &&
947:           Boolean(
948:             activation &&
949:             this.paths &&
950:             candidate.componentRoot &&
951:             toolPathComparisonKey(candidate.componentRoot, this.platform) ===
952:               toolPathComparisonKey(
953:                 runtimeDirectory(this.paths, componentId, activation.activeVersion, this.platform, this.arch),
954:                 this.platform,
955:               ),
956:           ),
957:       );
958:       const installed = Boolean(activation);
959:       result[componentId] = {
960:         componentId,
961:         installed,
962:         activeVersion: activation?.activeVersion,
963:         availableVersion: component?.version,
964:         platformArch: variant ? `${variant.platform}-${variant.arch}` : activation?.platformArch,
965:         downloadBytes: variant?.downloadBytes,
966:         installedBytes: variant?.installedBytes,
967:         diskBytes: this.paths ? boundedDirectoryBytes(path.join(this.paths.runtimes, componentId)) : undefined,
968:         sourceName: component ? COMPONENT_SOURCE_NAMES[componentId] : undefined,
969:         licenseName: component?.license.name,
970:         licenseUrl: component?.license.url,
971:         health: installed
972:           ? healthy
973:             ? "healthy"
974:             : "modified"
975:           : variant
976:             ? "missing"
977:             : component
978:               ? "unsupported"
979:               : "missing",
980:         canInstall: Boolean(variant && (!installed || activation?.activeVersion !== component?.version)),
981:         canRepair: Boolean(variant && installed),
982:         canRemove: installed,
983:       };
984:     }
985:     return result;
986:   }

1001:   private applyDescriptorEnvironment(descriptor: CommandDescriptor): CommandDescriptor {
1002:     if (descriptor.provider !== "managed" || !this.paths) return descriptor;
1003:     if (descriptor.componentId === "node-lts") {
1004:       descriptor.envPatch = {
1005:         ...descriptor.envPatch,
1006:         npm_config_cache: this.paths.caches.npm,
1007:         npm_config_prefix: this.paths.prefixes.npm,
1008:       };
1009:     } else if (descriptor.componentId === "uv") {
1010:       descriptor.envPatch = {
1011:         ...descriptor.envPatch,
1012:         UV_CACHE_DIR: this.paths.caches.uv,
1013:         UV_TOOL_DIR: this.paths.prefixes.uvTools,
1014:         UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR: this.paths.bin,
1015:         UV_NO_MODIFY_PATH: "1",
1016:         UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS: "manual",
1017:       };
1018:     } else if (descriptor.componentId === "cpython") {
1019:       descriptor.envPatch = { ...descriptor.envPatch, PIP_REQUIRE_VIRTUALENV: "true" };
1020:     } else if (descriptor.componentId === "bun") {
1021:       descriptor.envPatch = {
1022:         ...descriptor.envPatch,
1023:         BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR: this.paths.caches.bun,
1024:       };
1025:     } else if (descriptor.componentId === "portable-git" && descriptor.componentRoot) {
1026:       if (descriptor.capability === "vcs.git") {
1027:         descriptor.pathEntries = portableGitNativePathEntries(descriptor.componentRoot);
1028:       } else if (descriptor.capability === "shell.bash") {
1029:         descriptor.shellPathEntries = portableGitShellPathEntries(descriptor.componentRoot);
1030:         descriptor.shellEnvPatch = portableGitShellEnvPatch();
1031:       }

460:     this.assertRun(record, runId);
461:     if (terminalState(record.state)) return this.publicInfo(record);
462:     if (source === "user") record.userStopBarrier = true;
463:     record.stopSource = source;
464:     record.state = "stopping";
465:     this.append(record, "system", `Stop requested by ${source} (${mode})`);
466:     this.emitChanged(record, "state");
467:     if (!record.backend) {
468:       record.state = "killed";
469:       record.stoppedAt = this.now();
470:       record.stdinOpen = false;
471:       record.exit = { code: null, reason: "stopped", stoppedBy: source, finishedAt: this.now() };
472:       record.finish?.resolve();
473:       this.emitChanged(record, "exit");
474:       return this.publicInfo(record);
475:     }
476:     try {
477:       await record.backend.stop(mode, source);
478:     } catch {
479:       // The timeout cleanup below disposes the backend containment.
480:     }
481:     try {
482:       await timeout(
483:         record.finish?.promise ?? Promise.resolve(),
484:         STOP_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_MS,
485:         "Managed process did not stop in time",
486:       );
487:     } catch (error) {
488:       await record.backend.dispose();
489:       if (!terminalState(record.state)) {
490:         this.containmentFailed = true;
491:         record.state = "lost";
492:         record.stoppedAt = this.now();
493:         record.stdinOpen = false;
494:         record.exit = { code: null, reason: "host-failure", stoppedBy: source, finishedAt: this.now() };
495:         this.append(record, "system", "Managed process cleanup could not be verified; new starts are disabled");
496:         this.emitChanged(record, "exit");
497:         record.finish?.resolve();
498:       }
499:       if (!terminalState(record.state)) {
500:         record.state = "killed";
501:         record.stoppedAt = this.now();
502:         record.exit = { code: null, reason: "stopped", stoppedBy: source, finishedAt: this.now() };
503:         this.emitChanged(record, "exit");
504:         record.finish?.resolve();
505:       }
506:       if (error instanceof ManagedProcessError && mode !== "force") {
507:         this.append(record, "system", "Graceful stop timed out; process tree was force terminated");
508:       }
509:     }
510:     return this.publicInfo(record);
511:   }

513:   async restart(
514:     processId: string,
515:     runId: string,
516:     source: "agent" | "user",
517:     ownerSessionId?: string,
518:     trusted = true,
519:   ): Promise<ManagedProcessPublicInfo> {
520:     const record = this.requireRecord(processId, ownerSessionId);
521:     this.assertRun(record, runId);
522:     if (source === "agent" && record.userStopBarrier) {
523:       throw new ManagedProcessError(
524:         "PROCESS_USER_STOPPED",
525:         "The user stopped this process; only a user restart can clear the barrier",
526:       );
527:     }
528:     if (!terminalState(record.state)) await this.stop(processId, runId, "graceful", source, ownerSessionId);
529:     this.assertRun(record, runId);
530:     if (source === "agent" && record.userStopBarrier) {
531:       throw new ManagedProcessError(
532:         "PROCESS_USER_STOPPED",
533:         "The user stopped this process; only a user restart can clear the barrier",
534:       );
535:     }
536:     if (source === "user") record.userStopBarrier = false;
537:     await this.assertStartEnabled();
538:     this.assertRun(record, runId);
539:     if (source === "agent" && record.userStopBarrier) {
540:       throw new ManagedProcessError(
541:         "PROCESS_USER_STOPPED",
542:         "The user stopped this process; only a user restart can clear the barrier",
543:       );
544:     }
545:     if (!trusted)
546:       throw new ManagedProcessError(
547:         "PROCESS_PROJECT_UNTRUSTED",
548:         "Project trust is required to restart a managed process",
549:       );
550: 
551:     record.generation += 1;
552:     record.restartCount += 1;
553:     record.runId = randomUUID();
554:     record.state = "restarting";
555:     record.readiness = record.readinessSpec.type === "none" ? "not-requested" : "pending";
556:     record.readinessMatched = undefined;
557:     record.startedAt = undefined;
558:     record.stoppedAt = undefined;
559:     record.exit = undefined;
560:     record.stdinOpen = true;
561:     record.endpoints = [];
562:     record.networkWarnings = managedProcessNetworkWarnings(record.command);
563:     record.output = new ManagedProcessOutputBuffer(record.runId);
564:     record.decoder = this.createDecoder(record);
565:     record.removeBackendListener?.();
566:     record.backend = undefined;
567:     record.removeBackendListener = undefined;
568:     record.finish = undefined;
569:     record.reaper = undefined;
570:     record.reaperRegistered = false;
571:     record.stopSource = undefined;
572:     record.stdinWindow = [];
573:     this.emitChanged(record, "state");
574:     try {
575:       await this.startRun(record, trusted);
576:       return this.publicInfo(record);
577:     } catch (error) {
578:       await this.cleanupFailedRun(record);
579:       if (!terminalState(record.state)) {
580:         record.state = "failed";
581:         record.exit = { code: null, reason: "error", finishedAt: this.now() };
582:         record.stoppedAt = this.now();
583:         this.append(record, "system", boundedSystemMessage(error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)));
584:         this.emitChanged(record, "exit");
585:       }
586:       throw toolchainError(error);
587:     }
588:   }

709:   private async assertStartEnabled(): Promise<void> {
710:     if (this.containmentFailed) {
711:       throw new ManagedProcessError(
712:         "PROCESS_TREE_REAP_FAILED",
713:         "Managed process containment failed; restart the app after reviewing the Processes panel",
714:       );
715:     }
716:     if (this.platform === "win32" && this.arch !== "x64") {
717:       throw new ManagedProcessError("PROCESS_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED", "Managed processes require Windows x64");
718:     }
719:     if (this.platform !== "darwin" && this.platform !== "linux" && this.platform !== "win32") {
720:       throw new ManagedProcessError(
721:         "PROCESS_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED",
722:         "Managed processes are not available on this platform",
723:       );
724:     }
725:     const setting = await this.parentCall<{
726:       enabled?: boolean;
727:       reaperReady?: boolean;
728:       capability?: ManagedProcessCapability;
729:       windowsHelper?: WindowsManagedProcessHelperDescriptor;
730:     }>("managedProcesses.getSettings", undefined, 5_000);
731:     if (!setting.enabled)
732:       throw new ManagedProcessError(
733:         setting.capability?.supported === true && setting.capability.ready === false
734:           ? "PROCESS_CONTAINMENT_UNAVAILABLE"
735:           : "PROCESS_FEATURE_DISABLED",
736:         setting.capability?.ready === false
737:           ? "Managed process containment is not ready"
738:           : "Enable Managed Processes in Settings first",
739:         setting.capability?.errorCode ? { subcode: setting.capability.errorCode } : undefined,
740:       );
741:     if (!setting.reaperReady) {
742:       throw new ManagedProcessError("PROCESS_CONTAINMENT_UNAVAILABLE", "Managed process crash recovery is not ready");
743:     }
744:     if (this.platform === "win32") {
745:       if (
746:         setting.capability?.backend !== "windows-job" ||
747:         setting.capability.ready !== true ||
748:         !setting.windowsHelper ||
749:         !getManagedProcessOwnerIdentity()
750:       ) {
751:         throw new ManagedProcessError(
752:           "PROCESS_CONTAINMENT_UNAVAILABLE",
753:           "Windows managed process containment is not ready",
754:           { subcode: setting.capability?.errorCode ?? "OWNER_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE" },
755:         );
756:       }
757:       this.windowsHelper = setting.windowsHelper;
758:     }
759:   }

761:   private assertStartBudget(ownerSessionId: string): void {
762:     const now = this.now();
763:     while (this.startTimes[0] !== undefined && now - this.startTimes[0] > START_RATE_WINDOW_MS) this.startTimes.shift();
764:     if (this.startTimes.length >= START_RATE_LIMIT) {
765:       throw new ManagedProcessError("PROCESS_LIMIT_REACHED", "Managed process start rate limit reached");
766:     }
767:     const active = [...this.records.values()].filter((record) => isManagedProcessActiveState(record.state));
768:     if (active.length >= MANAGED_PROCESS_LIMITS.globalActive) {
769:       throw new ManagedProcessError("PROCESS_LIMIT_REACHED", "Global managed process limit reached");
770:     }
771:     if (
772:       active.filter((record) => record.ownerSessionId === ownerSessionId).length >= MANAGED_PROCESS_LIMITS.sessionActive
773:     ) {
774:       throw new ManagedProcessError("PROCESS_LIMIT_REACHED", "Session managed process limit reached");
775:     }
776:     this.startTimes.push(now);
777:   }

779:   private async startRun(record: ManagedRecord, trusted: boolean, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<void> {
780:     record.state = "starting";
781:     record.finish = deferred();
782:     this.append(record, "system", `Starting ${record.label}`);
783:     this.emitChanged(record, "state");
784: 
785:     let context: ToolExecutionContext;
786:     try {
787:       context = await this.runtime.createExecutionContext({ cwd: record.cwd, intent: "managed-process", trusted });
788:       this.runtime.requireFromContext("shell.bash", context);
789:     } catch (error) {
790:       throw toolchainError(error);
791:     }
792:     this.assertStartNotCancelled(signal);
793:     if (record.stopSource !== undefined || terminalState(record.state)) {
794:       throw new ManagedProcessError("PROCESS_USER_STOPPED", "The managed process was stopped while starting");
795:     }
796:     const shell = this.runtime.requireFromContext("shell.bash", context);
797:     if (this.platform === "win32") {
798:       await this.startWindowsRun(record, context, shell, signal);
799:       return;
800:     }
801:     await this.startPosixRun(record, context, shell, signal);
802:   }

804:   private async startPosixRun(
805:     record: ManagedRecord,
806:     context: ToolExecutionContext,
807:     shell: CommandDescriptor,
808:     signal?: AbortSignal,
809:   ): Promise<void> {
810:     const backend = this.posixBackendFactory();
811:     record.backend = backend;
812:     record.removeBackendListener = backend.onEvent((event) => this.handleBackendEvent(record, backend, event));
813:     let prepared: Awaited<ReturnType<ManagedProcessBackend["prepare"]>>;
814:     try {
815:       prepared = await backend.prepare(
816:         {
817:           processId: record.processId,
818:           runId: record.runId,
819:           cwd: record.cwd,
820:           command: record.command,
821:           shell: {
822:             executable: shell.executable,
823:             argvPrefix: [...shell.argvPrefix],
824:             cwdSemantics: shell.cwdSemantics,
825:           },
826:           context,
827:         },
828:         signal,
829:       );
830:     } catch (error) {
831:       throw new ManagedProcessError(
832:         "PROCESS_CONTAINMENT_UNAVAILABLE",
833:         "POSIX managed process worker could not prepare containment",
834:         { subcode: boundedSystemMessage(error instanceof Error ? error.message : "WORKER_START_FAILED") },
835:       );
836:     }
837:     record.reaper = prepared.reaper;
838:     let journalRevision: number;
839:     try {
840:       const registered = await this.parentCall<{ journalRevision?: number }>(
841:         "managedProcesses.register",
842:         { record: prepared.reaper },
843:         5_000,
844:       );
845:       if (!Number.isSafeInteger(registered.journalRevision) || (registered.journalRevision ?? 0) <= 0) {
846:         throw new Error("Invalid journal revision");
847:       }
848:       journalRevision = registered.journalRevision!;
849:       record.reaperRegistered = true;
850:     } catch {
851:       await backend.dispose();
852:       throw new ManagedProcessError(
853:         "PROCESS_CONTAINMENT_UNAVAILABLE",
854:         "Could not register POSIX managed process crash recovery",
855:       );
856:     }
857:     try {
858:       await backend.commit(prepared, journalRevision);
859:     } catch (error) {
860:       await backend.dispose();
861:       throw new ManagedProcessError(
862:         "PROCESS_CONTAINMENT_UNAVAILABLE",
863:         "POSIX managed process worker could not commit containment",
864:         { subcode: boundedSystemMessage(error instanceof Error ? error.message : "WORKER_COMMIT_FAILED") },
865:       );
866:     }
867:     if (terminalState(record.state)) {
868:       await record.finish?.promise;
869:       return;
870:     }
871:     this.assertStartNotCancelled(signal);
872:     if (record.userStopBarrier) {
873:       await this.stop(record.processId, record.runId, "graceful", "user");
874:       throw new ManagedProcessError("PROCESS_USER_STOPPED", "The user stopped this process while it was starting");
875:     }
876:     if ((record.state as ManagedProcessState) !== "ready") record.state = "running";
877:     record.startedAt = this.now();
878:     this.emitChanged(record, "state");
879:   }

974:       try {
975:         await record.backend.dispose();

977:         this.containmentFailed = true;

997:       await this.parentCall(

1015:   private handleBackendEvent(
1016:     record: ManagedRecord,
1017:     backend: ManagedProcessBackend,
1018:     event: ManagedProcessBackendEvent,
1019:   ): void {
1020:     if (record.backend !== backend) return;
1021:     if (event.type === "stdout" || event.type === "stderr") {
1022:       record.decoder.write(event.type, event.bytes);
1023:       return;
1024:     }
1025:     if (event.type === "output-dropped") {
1026:       this.append(record, "system", `[system] Backend dropped ${event.bytes} bytes / ${event.chunks} chunks.`);
1027:       return;
1028:     }
1029:     if (event.type === "stdin-closed") {
1030:       record.stdinOpen = false;
1031:       this.emitChanged(record, "state");
1032:       return;
1033:     }
1034:     if (event.type === "stopping") {
1035:       this.append(record, "system", `Stopping phase: ${event.phase}`);

270:   register(value: unknown): { journalRevision: number } {
271:     if (!this.ready) throw new Error("Managed process reaper is not ready");
272:     const record = validateReaperRecord(value);
273:     const key = this.key(record);
274:     const existing = this.records.get(key);
275:     if (existing && existing.nonce !== record.nonce) throw new Error("Managed process reaper identity conflict");

282:     if (!value || typeof value !== "object" || Array.isArray(value))
283:       throw new Error("Invalid reaper unregister request");
284:     const request = value as { hostInstanceId?: unknown; processId?: unknown; runId?: unknown; nonce?: unknown };
285:     if (
286:       typeof request.hostInstanceId !== "string" ||
287:       typeof request.processId !== "string" ||
288:       typeof request.runId !== "string" ||
289:       typeof request.nonce !== "string"
290:     ) {
291:       throw new Error("Invalid reaper unregister request");
292:     }
293:     const key = `${request.processId}\0${request.runId}`;
294:     const existing = this.records.get(key);
295:     if (!existing) return { journalRevision: this.revision, removed: false };
296:     if (existing.hostInstanceId !== request.hostInstanceId || existing.nonce !== request.nonce) {
297:       throw new Error("Managed process reaper unregister identity mismatch");
298:     }
299:     this.records.delete(key);
300:     this.persist();

307:       (record) => !hostInstanceId || record.hostInstanceId === hostInstanceId,
308:     );
309:     const outcomes = await Promise.all(records.map(async (record) => ({ record, outcome: await this.reap(record) })));

314:       } else if (outcome === "identity-uncertain") {
315:         failure = "IDENTITY_UNCERTAIN";
316:       } else if (!failure) {
317:         failure = "REAP_FAILED";
318:       }

320:     if (failure) {
321:       this.ready = false;
322:       this.errorCode = failure;
323:     }

325:       this.persist();
326:     } catch {
327:       this.ready = false;
328:       this.errorCode = "JOURNAL_INVALID";
329:     }
330:     return this.status();

333:   private async reap(record: ManagedProcessReaperRecord): Promise<"removed" | "identity-uncertain" | "failed"> {
334:     if (record.platform === "win32") {
335:       if (this.platform !== "win32") return "identity-uncertain";
336:       try {
337:         const outcome = this.reapWindows
338:           ? (await this.reapWindows(record))
339:             ? "removed"
340:             : "failed"
341:           : this.windowsHelper
342:             ? await reapWindowsRecord(record, this.windowsHelper, this.log)
343:             : "failed";
344:         if (outcome === "removed") {
345:           this.log(`managed process reaped process=${this.safeId(record.processId)}`);
346:           return "removed";
347:         }
348:         return outcome;
349:       } catch {
350:         return "failed";
351:       }
352:     }
353:     if (this.platform === "win32") return "identity-uncertain";
354:     if (!this.groupExists(record.pgid)) return "removed";
355:     const fingerprint = await this.fingerprint(record.pid);
356:     if (!fingerprint || fingerprint !== record.startFingerprint) {
357:       this.log(`managed process reap refused identity mismatch process=${this.safeId(record.processId)}`);
358:       return "identity-uncertain";
359:     }
360:     const stopped = await this.terminateGroup(record.pgid, { interruptMs: 500, terminateMs: 1_000, forceMs: 1_000 });
361:     if (!stopped) {
362:       this.log(`managed process reap failed process=${this.safeId(record.processId)}`);
363:       return "failed";
364:     }
365:     this.log(`managed process reaped process=${this.safeId(record.processId)}`);
366:     return "removed";
367:   }

372:   }

375:     return `${record.processId}\0${record.runId}`;
376:   }

379:     return value.replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/gi, "").slice(-12);

329:           onError?: (error: { extensionPath: string; event: string; error: string }) => void;
330:         }) => Promise<void>;
331:         await bindExtensions.call(this.inner, {
332:           uiContext,
333:           mode: "rpc",
334:           commandContextActions: this.createExtensionCommandContextActions(),
335:           shutdownHandler: () =>
336:             this.emit({
337:               type: "extension_ui_request",
338:               id: randomUUID(),
339:               method: "notify",
340:               notifyType: "warning",
341:               message: "Extension requested shutdown, but shutdown is not supported in Pi Desktop.",
342:             } as ExtensionUiRequest as AgentEvent),
343:           onError: (error) =>
344:             this.emit({
345:               type: "extension_error",
346:               extensionPath: error.extensionPath,
347:               event: error.event,
348:               error: error.error,
349:             }),
350:         });
351:       } else {
352:         this.inner.extensionRunner.setUIContext?.(uiContext, "rpc");
353:       }
354:       this.extensionsBound = true;
355:       this.applyForcedEmptySystemPrompt();
356:       console.log(`[pi-desktop] session_start dispatched to extensions for session ${this.inner.sessionId}`);
357:     })()
358:       .catch((err) => {
359:         this.extensionBindingError = err;
360:         console.warn(
361:           `[pi-desktop] extension binding attempt ${attempt} failed after ${Date.now() - startedAt}ms for session ${this.inner.sessionId}`,
362:         );
363:         throw err;
364:       })
365:       .finally(() => {
366:         if (this.extensionBindingPromise === bindingPromise) this.extensionBindingPromise = null;
367:       });
368:     this.extensionBindingPromise = bindingPromise;
369: 
370:     return bindingPromise;
371:   }

380:       throw this.extensionBindingError instanceof Error

382:         : new Error(String(this.extensionBindingError));

425:   private enqueueTurn<T>(task: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
426:     this.queuedTurnCount += 1;
427:     notifyRunningChange();
428:     const run = this.turnTail
429:       .catch(() => undefined)
430:       .then(async () => {
431:         if (!this._alive) throw new Error("Agent session is no longer available");
432:         this.promptRunning = true;
433:         notifyRunningChange();
434:         try {
435:           return await task();
436:         } finally {
437:           this.promptRunning = false;
438:           this.queuedTurnCount = Math.max(0, this.queuedTurnCount - 1);
439:           notifyRunningChange();
440:         }
441:       });
442:     this.turnTail = run.then(
443:       () => undefined,
444:       () => undefined,
445:     );

449:   async runExternalTurn(params: {
450:     runId: string;
451:     message: string;
452:     channel: ChannelId;
453:     images?: Array<{ type: "image"; data: string; mimeType: string }>;
454:     channelAttachments?: ChannelMessageAttachment[];
455:     attachmentContext?: string;
456:     onProgress?: (event: AgentEvent) => void;
457:   }): Promise<{ runId: string; finalText: string }> {
458:     return this.enqueueTurn(async () => {
459:       this.emit({ type: "channel_turn_start", runId: params.runId });
460:       this.externalTurnActive = true;
461:       this.externalTurnChannel = params.channel;
462:       this.externalTurnAttachments = params.channelAttachments ?? null;
463:       setBrowserSessionSource(this.inner.sessionManager, "channel");
464:       browserAgentRuntime.beginTurn(this.sessionId, "channel");
465:       this.externalTurnProgress = params.onProgress ?? null;
466:       try {
467:         this.inner.sessionManager.appendCustomEntry("pi-desktop-channel-source", {
468:           runId: params.runId,
469:           channel: params.channel,
470:           ...(params.channelAttachments?.length ? { attachments: params.channelAttachments } : {}),
471:         });
472:         if (params.attachmentContext) {
473:           await this.inner.sendCustomMessage(
474:             {
475:               customType: "pi-desktop-channel-attachment-context",
476:               content: params.attachmentContext,
477:               display: false,
478:             },
479:             { deliverAs: "nextTurn" },
480:           );
481:         }
482:         await this.inner.prompt(params.message, {
483:           ...(params.images?.length ? { images: params.images } : {}),
484:           expandPromptTemplates: false,
485:           source: "rpc",
486:         });
487:         const finalText = this.inner.getLastAssistantText()?.trim() ?? "";
488:         this.emit({ type: "channel_turn_end", runId: params.runId, finalText });
489:         return { runId: params.runId, finalText };
490:       } catch (error) {
491:         try {
492:           this.inner.sessionManager.appendCustomEntry("pi-desktop-channel-source-cancelled", { runId: params.runId });
493:         } catch {
494:           // A best-effort UI marker must never hide the original turn failure.
495:         }
496:         this.emit({
497:           type: "channel_turn_error",
498:           runId: params.runId,
499:           errorMessage: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
500:         });
501:         throw error;
502:       } finally {
503:         this.externalTurnProgress = null;
504:         this.externalTurnActive = false;
505:         this.externalTurnChannel = null;
506:         this.externalTurnAttachments = null;
507:         setBrowserSessionSource(this.inner.sessionManager, "local");
508:       }
509:     });
510:   }

575:   async send(command: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<unknown> {
576:     this.resetIdleTimer();
577:     const type = command.type as string;
578:     if (this.shouldWaitForExtensions(type)) await this.waitForExtensionsBound();
579: 
580:     switch (type) {
581:       case "prompt": {
582:         // Fire and forget — events come via subscribe
583:         const promptImages = command.images as Array<{ type: "image"; data: string; mimeType: string }> | undefined;
584:         const streamingBehavior = command.streamingBehavior as "steer" | "followUp" | undefined;
585:         if (!streamingBehavior) browserAgentRuntime.beginTurn(this.sessionId, "local");
586:         const invokePrompt = () =>
587:           this.inner.prompt(command.message as string, {
588:             ...(promptImages?.length ? { images: promptImages } : {}),
589:             ...(streamingBehavior ? { streamingBehavior } : {}),
590:             source: "rpc",
591:           });
592:         const operation = streamingBehavior ? invokePrompt() : this.enqueueTurn(invokePrompt);
593:         operation
594:           .then(() => {
595:             if (!streamingBehavior) this.emit({ type: "prompt_done" });
596:           })
597:           .catch((error) => {
598:             this.emit({
599:               type: "prompt_error",
600:               errorMessage: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
601:             });
602:             if (!streamingBehavior) this.emit({ type: "prompt_done" });
603:           });
604:         return null;
605:       }
606: 
607:       case "abort":
608:         await this.withFinalRunningNotification(() => this.inner.abort());
609:         return null;
610: 
611:       case "get_state": {
612:         const model = this.inner.model;
613:         const contextUsage = this.inner.getContextUsage();
614:         return {
615:           sessionId: this.inner.sessionId,
616:           sessionFile: this.inner.sessionFile ?? "",
617:           isStreaming: this.inner.isStreaming,
618:           isPromptRunning: this.promptRunning,
619:           isCompacting: this.inner.isCompacting,
620:           autoCompactionEnabled: this.inner.autoCompactionEnabled,
621:           autoRetryEnabled: this.inner.autoRetryEnabled,
622:           model: model ? { id: model.id, provider: model.provider } : undefined,
623:           messageCount: 0,
624:           pendingMessageCount: this.inner.pendingMessageCount,
625:           queuedMessages: {
626:             steering: [...this.inner.getSteeringMessages()],
627:             followUp: [...this.inner.getFollowUpMessages()],
628:           },
629:           contextUsage: contextUsage
630:             ? { percent: contextUsage.percent, contextWindow: contextUsage.contextWindow, tokens: contextUsage.tokens }
631:             : null,
632:           systemPrompt: this.inner.agent.state?.systemPrompt ?? "",
633:           thinkingLevel: this.inner.agent.state?.thinkingLevel ?? "off",
634:           extensionStatuses: this.getExtensionStatuses(),
635:           extensionWidgets: this.getExtensionWidgets(),
636:         };
637:       }
638: 
639:       case "set_model": {
640:         const { provider, modelId } = command as { provider: string; modelId: string };
641:         const model = this.inner.modelRuntime.getModel(provider, modelId);
642:         if (!model) throw new Error(`Model not found: ${provider}/${modelId}`);
643:         await this.inner.setModel(model);
644:         return { id: model.id, provider: model.provider };
645:       }
646: 
647:       case "fork": {
648:         const entryId = command.entryId as string;
649:         const sessionManager = this.inner.sessionManager;
650:         const currentSessionFile = this.inner.sessionFile;
651: 
652:         if (!sessionManager.isPersisted()) return { cancelled: true };
653:         if (!currentSessionFile) throw new Error("Persisted session is missing a session file");
654: 
655:         const entry = sessionManager.getEntry(entryId);
656:         if (!entry) throw new Error("Invalid entry ID for forking");
657: 
658:         const sessionDir = sessionManager.getSessionDir();
659:         let newSessionFile: string;
660: 
661:         if (!entry.parentId) {
662:           // Fork before the first message: create an empty session linked to this one
663:           const newManager = SessionManager.create(sessionManager.getCwd(), sessionDir);
664:           newManager.newSession({ parentSession: currentSessionFile });
665:           newSessionFile = newManager.getSessionFile() as string;
666:         } else {
667:           // Fork after some history: copy path up to (but not including) the fork point
668:           const sourceManager = SessionManager.open(currentSessionFile, sessionDir);
669:           const forkedPath = sourceManager.createBranchedSession(entry.parentId);
670:           if (!forkedPath) throw new Error("Failed to create forked session");
671:           newSessionFile = forkedPath;
672:         }
673: 
674:         const newSessionId = SessionManager.open(newSessionFile, sessionDir).getSessionId();
675:         cacheSessionPath(newSessionId, newSessionFile);
676:         await this.dispose({ abort: true, reason: "fork" });
677:         return { cancelled: false, newSessionId };
678:       }
679: 
680:       case "navigate_tree": {
681:         const result = await this.inner.navigateTree(command.targetId as string, {});
682:         return { cancelled: result.cancelled };
683:       }
684: 
685:       case "set_thinking_level": {
686:         const level = command.level as string;
687:         this.inner.setThinkingLevel(level);
688:         // setThinkingLevel clamps xhigh→high for models where supportsXhigh()===false.
689:         // If the model has DeepSeek thinking compat (reasoningEffortMap maps xhigh→max),
690:         // force the state back so the compat layer can use it correctly.
691:         if (
692:           level === "xhigh" &&
693:           (this.inner.model as { compat?: { thinkingFormat?: string } } | null)?.compat?.thinkingFormat ===
694:             "deepseek" &&
695:           this.inner.agent?.state
696:         ) {
697:           this.inner.agent.state.thinkingLevel = "xhigh";
698:         }
699:         return null;
700:       }
701: 
702:       case "compact": {
703:         const result = await this.withFinalRunningNotification(() =>
704:           this.enqueueTurn(() => this.inner.compact(command.customInstructions as string | undefined)),
705:         );
706:         return result;
707:       }
708: 
709:       case "set_session_name": {
710:         const name = (command.name as string | undefined)?.trim();
711:         if (!name) throw new Error("Session name cannot be empty");
712:         this.inner.setSessionName(name);
713:         return null;
714:       }
715: 
716:       case "get_session_stats": {
717:         return {
718:           ...this.inner.getSessionStats(),
719:           sessionName: this.inner.sessionManager.getSessionName(),
720:         };
721:       }
722: 
723:       case "get_last_assistant_text": {
724:         return { text: this.inner.getLastAssistantText() ?? "" };
725:       }
726: 
727:       case "set_auto_compaction": {
728:         this.inner.setAutoCompactionEnabled(command.enabled as boolean);
729:         return null;
730:       }
731: 
732:       case "clear_queue": {
733:         // Full clear only: pi has no single-item dequeue, and clear+requeue
734:         // races against the agent loop pulling messages mid-flight.
735:         return this.inner.clearQueue();
736:       }
737: 
738:       case "steer": {
739:         const steerImages = command.images as Array<{ type: "image"; data: string; mimeType: string }> | undefined;
740:         await this.inner.steer(command.message as string, steerImages?.length ? steerImages : undefined);
741:         return null;
742:       }
743: 
744:       case "follow_up": {
745:         const followImages = command.images as Array<{ type: "image"; data: string; mimeType: string }> | undefined;
746:         await this.inner.followUp(command.message as string, followImages?.length ? followImages : undefined);
747:         return null;
748:       }
749: 
750:       case "get_tools": {
751:         const all: ToolInfo[] = this.inner.getAllTools();
752:         const active = new Set<string>(this.inner.getActiveToolNames());
753:         return all.map((t) => ({
754:           name: t.name,
755:           description: t.description,
756:           active: active.has(t.name),
757:         }));
758:       }
759: 
760:       case "get_commands": {
761:         const commands: SlashCommandInfo[] = [];
762:         for (const registered of this.inner.extensionRunner.getRegisteredCommands()) {
763:           commands.push({
764:             name: registered.invocationName,
765:             description: registered.description,
766:             source: "extension",
767:             sourceInfo: registered.sourceInfo,
768:           });
769:         }
770:         for (const template of this.inner.promptTemplates) {
771:           commands.push({
772:             name: template.name,
773:             description: template.description,
774:             source: "prompt",
775:             sourceInfo: template.sourceInfo,
776:           });
777:         }
778:         for (const skill of this.inner.resourceLoader.getSkills().skills) {
779:           commands.push({
780:             name: `skill:${skill.name}`,
781:             description: skill.description,
782:             source: "skill",
783:             sourceInfo: skill.sourceInfo,
784:           });
785:         }
786:         return { commands };
787:       }
788: 
789:       case "set_tools": {
790:         const toolNames = command.toolNames as string[];
791:         this.applyRequestedTools(toolNames);
792:         this.persistToolNames(this.sessionId, toolNames);
793:         return null;
794:       }
795: 
796:       case "reload": {
797:         await this.enqueueTurn(() => this.reloadSessionResources());
798:         this.syncBrowserToolActivation();
799:         return { success: true };
800:       }
801: 
802:       case "abort_compaction": {
803:         this.inner.abortCompaction();
804:         return null;
805:       }
806: 
807:       case "extension_ui_response": {
808:         this.resolveExtensionUiResponse(command as ExtensionUiResponse);
809:         return null;
810:       }
811: 
812:       case "extension_ui_input": {
813:         this.handleExtensionUiInput(command.id as string, command.data as string);
814:         return null;
815:       }
816: 
817:       case "set_auto_retry": {
818:         this.inner.setAutoRetryEnabled(command.enabled as boolean);
819:         return null;
820:       }
821: 
822:       default:
823:         throw new Error(`Unsupported command: ${type}`);
824:     }
825:   }

827:   /**
828:    * Stop the underlying agent and release resources. Calls are idempotent and
829:    * concurrent owners share one teardown attempt.
830:    */
831:   dispose(options: { abort?: boolean; reason?: string; timeoutMs?: number } = {}): Promise<void> {
832:     if (this.disposePromise) return this.disposePromise;
833:     const abort = options.abort !== false;
834:     const reason = options.reason ?? "explicit";
835:     const timeoutMs = options.timeoutMs ?? 5_000;
836:     this.destroy();
837: 
838:     this.disposePromise = (async () => {
839:       const teardown = async () => {
840:         if (abort) {
841:           try {
842:             await this.inner.abort();
843:           } catch (error) {
844:             console.warn(
845:               `[pi-desktop] session abort failed during ${reason} for ${this.sessionId}: ${error instanceof Error ? error.name : "UnknownError"}`,
846:             );
847:           }
848:         }
849:         const agent = this.inner.agent as { waitForIdle?: () => Promise<void>; dispose?: () => void | Promise<void> };
850:         try {
851:           await agent.waitForIdle?.();
852:         } catch (error) {
853:           console.warn(
854:             `[pi-desktop] session waitForIdle failed during ${reason} for ${this.sessionId}: ${error instanceof Error ? error.name : "UnknownError"}`,
855:           );
856:         }
857:         try {
858:           await agent.dispose?.();
859:         } catch (error) {
860:           console.warn(
861:             `[pi-desktop] session dispose failed during ${reason} for ${this.sessionId}: ${error instanceof Error ? error.name : "UnknownError"}`,
862:           );
863:         }
864:       };
865: 
866:       let timeout: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
867:       try {
868:         await Promise.race([
869:           teardown(),
870:           new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
871:             timeout = setTimeout(() => {
872:               console.warn(`[pi-desktop] session teardown timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms during ${reason}`);
873:               resolve();
874:             }, timeoutMs);
875:           }),
876:         ]);
877:       } finally {
878:         if (timeout) clearTimeout(timeout);
879:       }
880:     })();
881:     return this.disposePromise;
882:   }
883: 
884:   async abortAndDispose(): Promise<void> {
885:     await this.dispose({ abort: true, reason: "explicit" });
886:   }

888:   destroy(): void {
889:     if (!this._alive) return;
890:     this._alive = false;
891:     browserAgentRuntime.clearSession(this.sessionId);
892:     if (this.idleTimer) clearTimeout(this.idleTimer);
893:     this.unsubscribe?.();
894:     this.unsubscribe = null;
895:     for (const pending of this.pendingUiResponses.values()) pending.cancel();
896:     for (const id of Array.from(this.activeCustomUis.keys())) this.closeCustomUi(id, undefined);
897:     this.pendingUiResponses.clear();
898:     this.pendingUiRequests.clear();
899:     this.listeners = [];
900:     const destroyCallbacks = [...this.destroyCallbacks];
901:     this.destroyCallbacks.clear();
902:     for (const callback of destroyCallbacks) {
903:       try {
904:         callback();
905:       } catch {
906:         /* isolate teardown owners */
907:       }
908:     }
909:     notifyRunningChange();
910:   }

5: type VaultFile = {

10: function validateKey(key: string): string {
11:   const trimmed = key.trim();
12:   if (!/^channel:(weixin|telegram|feishu):[a-z0-9._-]{1,160}$/i.test(trimmed)) {
13:     throw new Error("Invalid channel credential key");

17: 
18: export class CredentialVault {
19:   constructor(private readonly filePath: string) {}
20: 
21:   private read(): VaultFile {
22:     try {
23:       const parsed = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(this.filePath, "utf8")) as Partial<VaultFile>;
24:       if (parsed.version !== 1 || !parsed.entries || typeof parsed.entries !== "object") {
25:         throw new Error("Invalid credential vault format");
26:       }
27:       return { version: 1, entries: parsed.entries };
28:     } catch (error) {
29:       if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") return { version: 1, entries: {} };
30:       throw error;
31:     }
32:   }
33: 
34:   private write(data: VaultFile): void {
35:     fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(this.filePath), { recursive: true });
36:     const temp = `${this.filePath}.${process.pid}.${Date.now()}.tmp`;
37:     fs.writeFileSync(temp, JSON.stringify(data, null, 2), { encoding: "utf8", mode: 0o600 });
38:     fs.renameSync(temp, this.filePath);
39:     try {
40:       fs.chmodSync(this.filePath, 0o600);
41:     } catch {
42:       /* best effort on Windows */
43:     }
44:   }
45: 
46:   private assertAvailable(): void {
47:     if (!safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()) {
48:       throw new Error("OS credential encryption is unavailable; channel credentials were not persisted");
49:     }
50:   }
51: 
52:   get(key: string): Record<string, unknown> | null {
53:     this.assertAvailable();
54:     const encrypted = this.read().entries[validateKey(key)];
55:     if (!encrypted) return null;
56:     const plaintext = safeStorage.decryptString(Buffer.from(encrypted, "base64"));
57:     const parsed = JSON.parse(plaintext) as unknown;
58:     if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== "object" || Array.isArray(parsed))
59:       throw new Error("Invalid channel credential payload");
60:     return parsed as Record<string, unknown>;
61:   }
62: 
63:   set(key: string, value: Record<string, unknown>): void {
64:     this.assertAvailable();
65:     const data = this.read();
66:     const encrypted = safeStorage.encryptString(JSON.stringify(value));
67:     data.entries[validateKey(key)] = encrypted.toString("base64");
68:     this.write(data);
69:   }
70: 
71:   delete(key: string): void {
72:     const data = this.read();
73:     delete data.entries[validateKey(key)];
74:     this.write(data);

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Practical guide to setting up a development environment, running the Electron app, building, packaging, and testing Pi Agent Desktop, with pointers to the architecture and operations guides.
instructions: Cover local development setup (Node 22.19+, npm ci, npm run dev), the build pipeline, the full verify gate, packaging for each platform, and how sessions/config live in ~/.pi/agent/.

pages.title: Architecture Overview
pages.purpose: Explain the Electron three-process architecture: Main process, Agent Host utilityProcess, and sandboxed React Renderer, plus the typed MessagePort RPC contract and persistence surface.
instructions: Explain responsibility boundaries across Main / Agent Host / Renderer, the MessagePort handoff through preload, host supervision/restart, and the no-TCP-surface principle. Describe the data/control flow for a typical session prompt.

pages.title: RPC Contract and System API
pages.purpose: Document the typed request/response and event-stream RPC contract that connects Renderer to Agent Host, the five wire message kinds, leases, timeouts, and how main bridges host->main calls.
instructions: Describe Api.method/Streams, the RpcWriter/response/event wire kinds, subscription semantics, leases, call timeouts, and the host->main (callMain) path used for browser, toolchain, and credential operations.

pages.title: Agent Host Supervision and Resilience
pages.purpose: Document how the Main process supervises the Agent Host utilityProcess: crash detection, restart budget, heartbeats, managed-process pre-restart gate, and Host/Renderer recovery flows.
instructions: Explain restart-on-crash with CRASH_WINDOW_MS/MAX_RESTARTS, ping timeout kill, snapshot acknowledgements (toolchain/browser), the renderer reconnect flow on host restart/crash, and the managed-process containment gate before restart.

pages.title: Agent Sessions and Project Workflows
pages.purpose: Explain how the Agent Host creates, manages, and persists Pi agent sessions, builds context pages, auto-titles sessions, forks, manages worktrees, session lists/indexing, and file watchers.
instructions: Explain session lifecycle, the in-process AgentSessionWrapper, queueing/steer/follow-up, session file persistence under ~/.pi/agent/sessions, session path cache, indexing/fingerprinting, and allowed-root file access policy.

pages.title: Configuration, Models, and Credentials
pages.purpose: Document model/provider configuration, model catalog refresh, credential storage via the CredentialVault and Pi credential sync, theme/ui state, and channel credential persistence.
instructions: Explain models.json location, atomic writes with conflict detection, model refresh coordinator with timeout/cancel, enabled-model preferences, credential vault encryption via safeStorage, and ui-state persistence.

pages.title: Persistence and State Surface
pages.purpose: Catalog where Pi Agent Desktop persists state: sessions, models.json, agent config in ~/.pi/agent, credential vault, browser settings/grants/secrets, toolchain state, and managed-process reaper journal.
instructions: Enumerate the key persisted files, their owners, write patterns (atomic temp+rename, mode 0o600), versioning/conflict checks, and what happens on corruption or missing encryption availability.

pages.title: Managed Background Processes (Agent Host)
pages.purpose: Document the managed background-process service in the Agent Host: lifecycle, states, readiness, output buffering, policy limits, LAN-bind confirmation, stop modes, and Windows/POSIX backends.
instructions: Explain how process_* agent tools start/manage processes, output buffering and cursors, start rate/active limits, readiness detection, user-stop barriers, POSIX process groups vs Windows Job Object, and command-blocking heuristics.

pages.title: Managed Process Crash Recovery (Reaper)
pages.purpose: Document the Main-process ManagedProcessReaper, journal persistence, identity fingerprinting, POSIX process-group reaping, and the Windows helper/Job Object recovery path.
instructions: Explain reaper readiness, journal v2 records, identity checks via start fingerprint, reap outcomes, fail-closed containment when cleanup cannot be confirmed, Windows helper secure directory and provenance, and quit/update cleanup.

pages.title: Built-in Browser Service
pages.purpose: Document the Main-owned WebContentsView browser: profiles, tabs, agent authorization, policy engine, network interception, downloads, secret vault, and advanced browser mode.
instructions: Explain browser settings/policy versioning, permission model (none/read/interact/advanced), runtime grants + leases, user takeover, network interception and header rules, advanced mode with CDP/cookies/UA, private-network protection, and the unresolved cookies gate.

pages.title: Messaging Channels (Weixin, Telegram, Feishu/Lark)
pages.purpose: Document the messaging-channel subsystem in the Agent Host: adapters, inbound processing, pairing, bindings, per-session workspaces, outbound rendering, and media staging.
instructions: Explain channel account/config/secret persistence, QR login flows, pairing TTL, inbound policy decisions, lane-scheduled sequential processing, bindings to Pi sessions, and per-channel outbound/media specifics.

pages.title: Developer Toolchains (Discovery and Managed Runtimes)
pages.purpose: Document the toolchain subsystem: capability discovery from system/bundled/managed sources, probing, candidate selection, project resolution, and app-private managed runtime install/repair/remove.
instructions: Explain capability IDs, provider priority, probing/verification, preference modes, per-project resolution caching, managed component lifecycle, and how executions consume resolved command descriptors and environment patches.

pages.title: Updates and Packaging
pages.purpose: Document the update pipeline (electron-updater adapter, update manager state machine, install protocol), platform packaging targets, and update integrity/limitations.
instructions: Explain the update state machine (check/download/install with busy, offset, signature/integrity), automatic check scheduling, install capacity gating on running sessions and managed processes, and platform/artifact packaging.

pages.title: Logging and Diagnostics
pages.purpose: Document the main logger, log rotation/redaction, diagnostics export, crash reporting, and packaged startup validation reports.
instructions: Explain the rotating main.log, sanitization/redaction, diagnostics archive export, crash reporter upload-to-server false, and the packaged-startup/custom validation report files.

pages.title: Testing and Quality Gates
pages.purpose: Document the test runner, verify gate pipeline, contract/security/i18n checks, managed-process workflow tests, Electron smoke tests, and how to run focused tests.
instructions: Explain node:test discovery under src/**/*.test.mjs, the verify pipeline order, and where each check lives. Note that unit tests run in Node without a GPU/display and that Electron integration tests are separate scripts.

pages.title: Change Guide: Main Process and IPC
pages.purpose: Focused guide for safely adding or changing Main-process behavior and the Renderer-Host IPC surface, with verification steps.
instructions: Walk through adding a new desktop IPC channel (contract type, preload method, main handler with trusted sender guard), adding an Agent Host Api/Stream, and how to run the contract-coverage and related checks.

149:  * The dir name is the sanitized branch name — close enough for display.
150:  */
151: function inferRemovedWorktree(cwd: string): ProjectInfo | null {
152:   const parent = dirname(cwd);
153:   if (!parent.endsWith("-worktrees")) return null;
154:   const repoRoot = parent.slice(0, -"-worktrees".length);
155:   if (!repoRoot || !existsSync(join(repoRoot, ".git"))) return null;
156:   return { projectRoot: repoRoot, branch: basename(cwd), isWorktree: true, isTopLevel: true };
157: }
158: 
159: export async function resolveProject(cwd: string): Promise<ProjectInfo> {
160:   const cache = getProjectCache();
161:   const cached = cache.get(cwd);
162:   if (cached && cached.expiresAt > Date.now()) return cached.info;
163: 
164:   let info: ProjectInfo;
165:   try {
166:     if (!existsSync(cwd)) {
167:       info = inferRemovedWorktree(cwd) ?? { projectRoot: cwd, branch: null, isWorktree: false, isTopLevel: false };
168:       cache.set(cwd, { info, expiresAt: Date.now() + PROJECT_CACHE_TTL_MS });
169:       return info;
170:     }
171:     const out = await git(cwd, [
172:       "rev-parse",
173:       "--path-format=absolute",
174:       "--git-common-dir",
175:       "--git-dir",
176:       "--show-toplevel",
177:       "--abbrev-ref",
178:       "HEAD",
179:     ]);
180:     const [commonDir, gitDir, toplevel, ref] = out.split("\n").map((l) => l.trim());
181:     // git prints resolved (symlink-free) paths; normalize cwd the same way
182:     let realCwd = cwd;
183:     try {
184:       realCwd = realpathSync(cwd);
185:     } catch {
186:       /* keep as-is */
187:     }
188:     // For a linked worktree, --git-dir differs from --git-common-dir.
189:     // Only collapse *worktree toplevels* into the main repo. A session whose
190:     // cwd is a subdirectory of a repo keeps its own project identity —
191:     // grouping subdirs under the repo root would change where new sessions
192:     // are created for existing users.
193:     const isTopLevel = worktreePathsEqual(toplevel, realCwd);
194:     const isWorktreeTopLevel = !worktreePathsEqual(gitDir, commonDir) && isTopLevel;
195:     info = {
196:       // Every toplevel resolves to a git-reported path so the projectRoot
197:       // format is identical regardless of how cwd was spelled (git prints
198:       // forward slashes on Windows; a restored session cwd may use
199:       // backslashes). Session filtering compares projectRoot strings, so a
200:       // separator mismatch would hide a project's sessions. For the main
201:       // checkout use toplevel rather than dirname(commonDir): in a submodule
202:       // commonDir lives under the superproject's .git/modules.
203:       projectRoot: isWorktreeTopLevel ? dirname(commonDir) : isTopLevel ? toplevel : cwd,
204:       branch: ref && ref !== "HEAD" ? ref : null,
205:       isWorktree: isWorktreeTopLevel,
206:       isTopLevel,
207:     };
208:   } catch {
209:     info = { projectRoot: cwd, branch: null, isWorktree: false, isTopLevel: false };
210:   }
211: 
212:   cache.set(cwd, { info, expiresAt: Date.now() + PROJECT_CACHE_TTL_MS });
213:   return info;
214: }
215: 
216: // ============================================================================
217: // Worktree operations
218: //
219: // These take any directory inside the repo (a worktree, the main checkout, or
220: // a subdirectory) and resolve the main repo root themselves via the git
221: // common dir, so callers can pass session cwds directly.
222: // ============================================================================
223: 
224: /** Main repo root (parent of the shared .git dir), or throws for non-git dirs */
225: async function getRepoRoot(cwd: string): Promise<string> {
226:   const commonDir = await git(cwd, ["rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir"]);
227:   return dirname(commonDir);
228: }
229: 
230: export async function listWorktrees(cwd: string): Promise<WorktreeInfo[]> {
231:   const out = await git(cwd, ["worktree", "list", "--porcelain"]);
232:   const worktrees: WorktreeInfo[] = [];
233:   let current: (Partial<WorktreeInfo> & { prunable?: boolean }) | null = null;
234: 
235:   const flush = () => {
236:     if (current?.path) {
237:       // Prunable worktrees point at missing/broken gitdirs and cannot be
238:       // browsed or selected usefully. Also skip vanished paths even if git has
239:       // not marked them prunable yet.
240:       if (!current.prunable && existsSync(current.path)) {
241:         worktrees.push({
242:           path: current.path,
243:           branch: current.branch ?? null,
244:           isMain: worktrees.length === 0,
245:         });
246:       }
247:     }
248:     current = null;
249:   };
250: 
251:   for (const line of out.split("\n")) {
252:     if (line.startsWith("worktree ")) {
253:       flush();
254:       current = { path: line.slice("worktree ".length).trim() };
255:     } else if (line.startsWith("branch ") && current) {
256:       current.branch = line
257:         .slice("branch ".length)
258:         .trim()
259:         .replace(/^refs\/heads\//, "");
260:     } else if (line.startsWith("prunable") && current) {
261:       current.prunable = true;
262:     } else if (line.trim() === "") {
263:       flush();
264:     }
265:   }
266:   flush();
267:   return worktrees;
268: }
269: 
270: function sanitizeBranchForDir(branch: string): string {
271:   return branch.replace(/[\/\\:*?"<>|\s]+/g, "-").replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "");
272: }
273: 
274: export async function addWorktree(cwd: string, branch: string): Promise<{ path: string; branch: string }> {
275:   const trimmed = branch.trim();
276:   if (!trimmed) throw new Error("Branch name is required");
277: 
278:   const dirName = sanitizeBranchForDir(trimmed);
279:   if (!dirName) throw new Error(`Invalid branch name: ${branch}`);
280: 
281:   const repoRoot = await getRepoRoot(cwd);
282:   const baseDir = `${resolve(repoRoot)}-worktrees`;
283:   const worktreePath = join(baseDir, dirName);
284:   if (existsSync(worktreePath)) {
285:     throw new Error(`Directory already exists: ${worktreePath}`);
286:   }
287:   mkdirSync(baseDir, { recursive: true });
288: 
289:   // Reuse the branch if it already exists, otherwise create it at HEAD.
290:   let branchExists = false;
291:   try {
292:     await git(repoRoot, ["rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", `refs/heads/${trimmed}`]);
293:     branchExists = true;
294:   } catch {
295:     branchExists = false;
296:   }
297: 
298:   try {
299:     if (branchExists) {
300:       await git(repoRoot, ["worktree", "add", "--", worktreePath, trimmed]);
301:     } else {
302:       await git(repoRoot, ["worktree", "add", "-b", trimmed, "--", worktreePath]);
303:     }
304:   } catch (error) {
305:     throw new Error(extractGitError(error));
306:   }
307: 
308:   allowFileRoot(worktreePath);
309:   invalidateProjectCache();
310:   return { path: worktreePath, branch: trimmed };
311: }
312: 
313: export async function removeWorktree(cwd: string, worktreePath: string, force = false): Promise<void> {
314:   const worktrees = await listWorktrees(cwd);
315:   const target = worktrees.find((w) => worktreePathsEqual(w.path, worktreePath));
316:   if (!target) throw new Error(`Not a worktree of this repository: ${worktreePath}`);
317:   if (target.isMain) throw new Error("Cannot remove the main worktree");
318: 
319:   try {
320:     await git(cwd, ["worktree", "remove", ...(force ? ["--force"] : []), target.path]);
321:   } catch (error) {
322:     throw new Error(extractGitError(error));
323:   }
324:   invalidateProjectCache();
325: }
326: 
327: function extractGitError(error: unknown): string {
328:   const stderr = (error as { stderr?: string }).stderr;
329:   if (typeof stderr === "string" && stderr.trim()) return stderr.trim();
330:   return error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
331: }

---
type: reference
title: Agent Sessions and Project Workflows
description: How the Pi Agent Desktop Agent Host creates, runs, persists, lists, and indexes Pi agent sessions, plus project/worktree resolution and file-access policy.
tags: [agent-host, sessions, project, worktree, indexing, rpc]
---

# Agent Sessions and Project Workflows

This page describes how the Agent Host (the `utilityProcess` that runs Pi
Coding Agent in-process) owns agent sessions scrub, how sessions are created,
run, persisted, listed, indexed, and auto-titled, and how project/worktree
resolution and the file-access policy work.

## Responsibility and ownership

Session management lives entirely in the Agent Host process under
`src/agent-host/`. The Renderer never touches `pi-coding-agent` directly; it
sends session commands over the typed `MessagePort` RPC contract
(`src/contract/api.ts`) and receives streamed events back. The Main process
supervises the Host process but does not manage sessions.

Two layers own session state:

- The **RPC session registry** (`src/agent-host/rpc-manager.ts`) keeps in-memory
  `AgentSessionWrapper` objects for live sessions, deduplicates starts with
  per-session locks, broadcasts running-session-id changes, and disposes every
  live wrapper on process `exit`/`SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` (`rpc-manager.ts:1324-1333`).
- The **disk index** (`src/agent-host/session-index.ts`) builds a fingerprint
  cache of session files under the Pi agent directory so listing is cheap and
  watcher-driven.

## Where sessions persist

Session files live under the Pi agent directory (`~/.pi/agent/sessions` unless
overridden by `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`), which is the same location the Pi
CLI uses. `session-watcher.ts:28` resolves the root from
`process.env.PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR || getAgentDir() + "sessions"`.
Because the desktop app reuses Pi's session/config directory, users who already
run Pi CLI can reuse existing sessions without migration.

The on-disk format is owned by `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`'s
`SessionManager`. Pi Desktop appends custom entries to sessions for its own
markers — for example a `pi-desktop-channel-source` entry recording a messaging
channel turn and a `pi-desktop-session-tools` entry persisting the enabled tool
set (`rpc-manager.ts:467`, `rpc-manager.ts:94-110`).

## Session lifecycle

### Creation

`agent.new` in `handlers.ts` validates a project `cwd`, starts a session through
`startRpcSession` (`rpc-manager.ts`), allows that root for file access, binds
streaming events once via `ensureSessionEvents`, optionally sets a model and
thinking level, and either sends an initial command or (for
`type: "ensure_session"`) returns with no turn.

`startRpcSession` keyed by session id; for brand-new sessions Pi generates its
own id. It loads persisted tool names from the last `pi-desktop-session-tools`
custom entry when re-opening an existing session.

### Running a turn

The `AgentSessionWrapper` (`rpc-manager.ts:170`) wraps Pi's `AgentSessionLike`.
Its `send(command)` handler drives the agent. Prompts that are *not* given an
explicit `streamingBehavior` run through `enqueueTurn`, which serializes turns on
a `turnTail` promise chain and increments a queued-turn counter so the app can
report pending work (`rpc-manager.ts:425-447`). Steer and follow-up commands call
`inner.steer` / `inner.followUp` directly and run outside the serialized queue.

Event streaming flows through `inner.subscribe`; each event is re-broadcast to
RPC listeners and `notifyRunningChange()` pushes the running-session-id set.

### Command surface

The wrapper implements a broker for typed commands used by the renderer,
including `prompt`, `abort`, `get_state`, `set_model`, `fork`, `navigate_tree`,
`set_thinking_level`, `compact`, `set_session_name`, `get_session_stats`,
`get_tools`, `get_commands`, `set_tools`, `reload`, `steer`, `follow_up`, and
`extension_ui_response` (`send`), while serializing and reporting status for
`prompt`/`steer`/`follow_up`/`get_commands` via `shouldWaitForExtensions`
(`rpc-manager.ts:386-388`).

### Forking

`fork` in `send` either creates an empty linked session before the first message
or calls `createBranchedSession` to copy history up to (excluding) the fork
point, then disposes the current wrapper and returns the new session id
(`rpc-manager.ts:647-678`).

### Idle eviction and disposal

Every active wrapper has a 10-minute idle timer. When a session is not running
and idle, `dispose({ abort: true, reason: "idle-eviction" })` is called
(`rpc-manager.ts:542-555`). `dispose` is idempotent (all callers share one
teardown) and races teardown against a 5s default timeout. Deletion
(`sessions.delete`) aborts and disposes the live session before unlinking the
session file (`handlers.ts:1033-1046`).

## Session listing, reading, and indexing

`listAllSessions` (`session-reader.ts`) prefers the `sessionIndex` and falls
back to Pi's `SessionManager.listAll()` when the index is unavailable.

The session index (`session-index.ts`) fingerprints each session file by
`size/mtimeMs/ctimeMs/ino` and reuses the cached `SessionInfo` when the file is
unchanged (`session-index.ts:33-45`). `sessions.get` builds a `SessionDetail`
from the indexed snapshot plus a live `get_state` call when `includeState` is
set, and supports cursored history pages.

A session watcher (`session-watcher.ts`) `fs.watch`es the sessions root,
debounces changes 300ms, invalidates the allowed-roots cache, refreshes the
index, and emits `sessions.changed` events. It distinguishes a full refresh
from path-level refreshes and emits `deleted` when an indexed path disappears
(`session-watcher.ts:50-64`).

Session history reads use `session-history.ts` builders with an opaque,
version-stamped cursor; stale cursors surface as a `STALE_CURSOR` RPC error
(`handlers.ts:958-967`).

## Auto title generation

The Host can silently ask the configured model to title the session from the
first user message. `generateSessionTitle` in `handlers.ts` uses a short
system prompt, a 15s abort timeout, and `cacheRetention: "none"` so the request
never touches session history or writes prompt-cache entries
(`handlers.ts:416-480`). The result is sanitized via `sanitizeGeneratedTitle`
in `session-title.ts`; on any failure `makeFallbackTitle` reuses the first
characters of the first user message so the sidebar never shows an untitled
session.

A write is applied only if the session still has no name, using the same
synchronous-turn check so a manual rename that runs first is never overwritten
(`handlers.ts:499-551`).

## Project and worktree resolution

`src/shared/worktree.ts` resolves a `cwd` to a `ProjectInfo`:
`projectRoot`, current `branch`, whether the directory is a linked worktree, and
whether it is a checkout top level. For a linked worktree the project root is the
parent of the git *common dir* (the main repo), so all worktrees collapse onto
the shared project. Non-git directories resolve to themselves. Results are
cached 60s and invalidated eagerly on worktree add/remove.

`addWorktree` places new worktrees in `<repoRoot>-worktrees/<sanitized-branch>`
and `allowFileRoot`s the created path; `removeWorktree` refuses the main
worktree and propagates a dirty-tree error unless `force` is set
(`worktree.ts:274-325`). The wrapper checks that a worktree still contains no
active managed processes before removal via `handlers.ts`.

## File-access policy

All file reads in the Host are guarded by the allowed-roots policy
(`src/agent-host/file-access.ts`). Allowed roots are derived from every
session's `cwd` and `projectRoot`, plus `~` directories matching `pi-cwd-<date>`
and any roots added programmatically (`allowFileRoot`). The set is cached with a
TTL that is long (10 min) when the session watcher is healthy and short (5s)
otherwise (`allowed-roots.ts:60-70`). `files.*` handlers call `assertPathAllowed`
before acting (`handlers.ts:203-208`).

## Interaction with managed processes

Deleting a session refuses (with `CONFLICT`) while it still owns active managed
background processes unless `force` is set, in which case those processes are
stopped first. Removing a worktree likewise refuses while it contains active
managed processes (`handlers.ts:1017-1032`, `handlers.ts:1124-1132`).

## Failure behavior

- If the session index fails, `listAllSessions` falls back to Pi's own listing.
- If a live prompt rejects, the wrapper emits `prompt_error` and re-emits
  `prompt_done` so the renderer unblocks.
- If an external-channel turn rejects, a `channel_turn_error` event is emitted
  and the error propagates; the browser session source is reset to `local` in
  `finally`.
- Unhandled session wrapper disposal is isolated per owner via destroy
  callbacks.

## Tests

Focused unit tests exercise the pure helpers and policies (for example
`session-title`, `session-history`, `session-file-references`,
`project-tree`, `worktree`, `file-access`, `tool-environment`) under
`src/**/*.test.mjs`. They run in Node without a GPU.

---
type: reference
title: Configuration, Models, and Credentials
description: How Pi Agent Desktop stores and refreshes model/provider configuration, enabled-model preferences, credentials (CredentialVault, Pi credential sync), and UI state.
tags: [configuration, models, credentials, auth, ui-state]
---

# Configuration, Models, and Credentials

This page covers how Pi Agent Desktop stores and loads configuration: the
model/provider catalog and preferences, credential storage and synchronization,
theme / window / UI state, and channel credentials.

## Model configuration persistence

Model provider configuration lives in `models.json` in the Pi agent directory
(`~/.pi/agent/models.json` via `getAgentDir()`), shared with the Pi CLI
(`handlers.ts:210-212`).

Writes are conflict-checked and atomic:

- The Host reads a snapshot of the file together with a content version
  (`sha256` of the raw bytes, or the sentinel `"missing"` when the file is
  absent) (`handlers.ts:214-225`).
- `writeModelsJson` requires the version the Renderer saw to be unchanged
  before committing; otherwise it throws a `CONFLICT` RPC error so the editor's
  pending edits are not silently lost (`handlers.ts:241-247`).
- The new content is written to a `.<pid>.tmp` fileholistic then renamed over
  the target; the previous good file is copied to `models.json.bak` and the
  rename happens atomically (`handlers.ts:249-279`).
- A corrupt `models.json` produces a `PARSE_ERROR` RPC error (never a silent
  empty overwrite) (`handlers.ts:227-239`).

## Model catalog refresh

`ModelCatalogRefreshCoordinator` in `src/agent-host/model-runtime.ts` drives
on-demand refreshes of the model catalog. A refresh is keyed by both request id
and cwd; starting a new refresh replaces the previous one for that request id
and cwd, and the shared runtime refresh uses `allowNetwork: true, force: true`
(`model-runtime.ts:59-149`).

Key semantics:

- Each refresh runs under an `AbortController`, and a 12s hard timeout aborts
  it (`MODEL_CATALOG_REFRESH_TIMEOUT_MS`) (`model-runtime.ts:5`, `:87`).
- When `PI_OFFLINE` is set the coordinator skips network refresh and returns an
  `offline` catalog state.
- On timeout or abort, the most recent cached models remain available, and a
  warning is attached (`model-runtime.ts:125-143`). Per-provider failures each
  yield a `PROVIDER_REFRESH_FAILED` warning while the last known snapshot stays
  available (`resolveAvailableModels` in `handlers.ts:604-641`).
- `cancel(requestId)` aborts a specific refresh; `cancelAll()` aborts all.

The host keeps a single shared `ModelRuntime` (`getSharedModelRuntime`), while
each agent session gets its own cwd-bound session service so project
extensions cannot leak provider registrations across sessions
(`model-runtime.ts:173-189`). `reloadSharedModelRuntimeConfig` refreshes local
config (`allowNetwork: false`) once the shared runtime exists.

## Enabled-model preferences

Per-project enabled-model lists are stored via the Pi settings manager
`getEnabledModels` / `setEnabledModels`. `filterByExactEnabledModels` only shows
models whose `provider/id` (or bare `id`) is in the enabled set; a
thinking-level suffix (`off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`) is
stripped before comparison (`handlers.ts:316-344`). If no enabled model matches,
all available models are shown. Input references are normalized and validated
(at most 2000 entries) in `normalizeEnabledModelsInput`.

The default model/provider is the one from settings when it is visible in the
filtered list.

## Credentials

### Model/provider credentials

Provider API keys, OAuth tokens, and logout are managed through Pi's model
runtime via `auth.*` RPC methods. Credential mutations are verified against the
actual runtime state in `credential-sync.ts`:

- `credentialStateMatches` compares the current runtime credential list to the
  intended target.
- After writing a credential, if the model runtime state does not match and a
  refresh (`allowNetwork: false`) fails, the operation returns a warning
  `MODEL_SYNC_FAILED` rather than presenting success (`credential-sync.ts:26-48`).
- A `CredentialSynchronizationError` triggers an attempted recovery via
  `recoverCommittedCredential` before the mutation is reported
  (`handlers.ts:382-399`).

Credentials themselves are persisted by the Pi agent in `~/.pi/agent/`.
`auth.loginStart` kicks off an OAuth flow whose progress arrives on the
`auth.login` stream.

### Channel credentials (CredentialVault)

Channel (Weixin / Telegram / Feishu) secrets are stored in the Main process by
`CredentialVault` (`src/main/credential-vault.ts`) in
`<userData>/channels.secrets.json`. Values are encrypted with Electron
`safeStorage` and base64-wrapped; the file is written atomically with mode
`0o600` (`credential-vault.ts:34-44`). If `safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()`
is false the vault refuses to read or write (`credential-vault.ts:46-50`), so a
machine without OS encryption never silently drops credentials.

Keys are restricted to the pattern
`channel:(weixin|telegram|feishu):<safe-id>` (`credential-vault.ts:10-15`). The
Host accesses it only through the `channelSecrets.*` request handler bridged by
Main (`host-manager.ts` request handler), so tokens never travel over the
Renderer RPC surface.

### Browser secrets

Advanced-browser-mode secrets (proxy credentials, header-rule secrets) are held
in a separate `BrowserSecretVault` (`src/main/browser/browser-secret-vault.ts`)
in `<userData>/browser-secrets.json`, also `safeStorage`-encrypted and
ref-addressed; see the browser service page.

## UI state

`src/main/window-state.ts` persists UI state to `<userData>/ui-state.json`:
window bounds / maximized flag (debounced 400ms while moving/resizing,
immediate on close), sidebar width, theme (`light`/`dark`/`system`), recent
cwds, background mode, and `automaticUpdateChecks` (`window-state.ts:40-70`).
`loadUiState` tolerates a missing/corrupt file by returning `{}`.

The theme is applied by setting `nativeTheme.themeSource` from the persisted
value at startup (`main.ts`), and the renderer can change it through
`desktop:set-theme-source`.

`desktop:set-ui-state` only accepts a validated patch
(`validateDesktopUiStatePatch`) before persisting (`ipc.ts:301-303`). Toolchain
settings (managed-runtime install preferences etc.) are persisted separately by
the toolchain state store under the app-private toolchain directory; see the
developer-toolchains page.

## Channel configuration

Channel accounts/bindings and login state are persisted by the channel config
store and state store in the Host data directory
(`~/.pi/desktop/channels.json`, `channels.state.json`, and staged media under
`channel-media`). Secrets never go in these files — see the messaging-channels
page.

## Verification

Invariants for configuration correctness are exercised by focused unit tests
(for example `credential-sync`, `model-runtime` helpers, `window-state-core`)
plus the contract-coverage gate (`scripts/check-contract-coverage.mjs`).
